## The question

[Use the beta variant](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/191759/use-the-beta-variant), asked by [z̫͋](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/59186/z%cc%ab%cd%8b) on TeX Stack Exchange (2014-07-16; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Is it possible to use the curled beta: ϐ (U+03D0) in a formula?
>
> There are variants available for `\epsilon`, `\theta`, `\phi`, `\rho`, `\sigma` and `\phi` with `\varepsilon`, `\vartheta`, etc... but there is no `\varbeta`. Why is that?
:::

You can with XeLaTeX and the [`mathspec`](http://ctan.org/pkg/mathspec) package:

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{mathspec}
\setmathfont(Greek){Cambria Math}

\begin{document}
$\alpha^2 + \varbeta^2 =\gamma^2$
\end{document}
```

![sample code output][1]

Here `Cambria Math` can be replaced by any font on your filesystem that supports this character.  Fileformat.info has a [list of all known fonts supporting it][2] and a [list of locally installed fonts that support it][3].

As egreg notes, you can also do it with the [`unicode-math`](http://ctan.org/pkg/unicode-math) package:

```latex
\documentclass{standalone}
\usepackage{unicode-math}
\setmathfont[math-style=TeX]{Cambria Math}
\newcommand{\varbeta}{ϐ}
\begin{document}
$\alpha^2 + \varbeta^2 =\gamma^2$
\end{document}
```


  [1]: abW49.png
  [2]: http://www.fileformat.info/info/unicode/char/3d0/fontsupport.htm
  [3]: http://www.fileformat.info/info/unicode/font/fontlist.htm?text=%CF%90%20-%20GREEK%20BETA%20SYMBOL%20%28U%2B03D0%29
